split_info.cv_design: stratified 5-fold within the train partition, group-aware on patient_id
split_info.horizon_gap_note: not a forecasting task - forecast_horizons holds a single value, so no origin gap is required. On a multi-horizon forecast this carries max(forecast_horizons) periods measured between the last train ORIGIN and the first validation ORIGIN (not between targets), names the horizon that set it, and records the rows dropped in between.
split_info.holdout_representativeness: Rows are drawn from one population and the split is random rather than temporal, so there is no drift argument. Validation is nonetheless reused across every iteration while the external holdout is scored once, so these figures are expected to be mildly optimistic.
split_info.reasoning: Deployment situation simulated: scoring new patients drawn from the same population. Neither boundary lands anywhere meaningful - the split is random within groups. A reasonable person might have split by admission date instead, to simulate forward deployment; not done here because EDA found no temporal trend in the target and the date coverage is only 14 months.
split_info.note: EDA reported grouping_structure (patients appear across multiple rows) - split by patient_id first, so every row for a given patient falls entirely into one partition, then assigned group-wise to approximate the target stratification. No _split column existed yet, so one was created and persisted with TWO partitions (train/validation); every later node reuses this exact assignment. There is no test partition: the held-out data was removed before this run began and is scored after the pipeline finishes. Validation absorbs the repeated per-iteration evaluation that Diagnosis reasons over, and every metric this run reports is a validation metric.

regime_coverage._note: Rows per identified regime per partition. A training partition holding 0% of a regime that validation or the expected holdout contains REJECTS the split — move to rolling origin so the last fold trains through the change, or move the boundary later.
regime_coverage.verdict: REJECTED in the example: train is 0% post-regime while the holdout is 100% post-regime. A model cannot learn a regime it has no examples of, and the failure is quiet because the pre-change validation rows carry the metrics.
